fields.intervention: Integrate a copper‑based anti‑fouling polymer coating onto the catheter surface that slowly releases biocides to inhibit clot and biofilm formation.
fields.expected_effect: Continuous inhibition of thrombus and biofilm buildup, maintaining flow patency for at least four weeks without heightened infection.
fields.falsification_test: In‑vitro flow loop comparing biocide‑coated catheters to standard catheters for clot formation over simulated 4‑week dialysis cycles.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on the catheter surface reduces thrombus formation, extending failure‑free survival.
fields.intervention: Apply a passive hydrophilic polymer (e.g., PEGylated) coating to the catheter lumen and exterior to create a low‑energy, non‑fouling surface that mimics the anticoagulant effect without active heparin.
fields.expected_effect: Decreased protein and platelet adhesion will limit intraluminal clot formation, preserving catheter flow patency for at least four weeks without raising infection risk.
fields.falsification_test: Randomize patients to receive hydrophilic‑polymer‑coated versus uncoated tunneled catheters and compare flow rates and occlusion incidence over 28 days; no improvement in the coated group would falsify the proposed mechanism.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on the catheter surface reduces thrombus formation, leading to longer failure‑free survival.
fields.intervention: Apply a heparin‑coated polymer layer to the catheter lumen and integrate a thin piezoelectric strip that emits low‑frequency ultrasonic waves (acoustic streaming) along the inner wall to synergistically inhibit clot adhesion.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained catheter patency for ≥4 weeks with a lower incidence of flow occlusion and no increase in infection risk.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a randomized bench‑top flow loop study comparing (a) heparin‑coated only catheters, (b) heparin‑coated + ultrasonic actuation catheters, and (c) non‑coated catheters; measure time to ≥50 % flow reduction under standardized blood-mimicking fluid over 28 days.

fields.mechanism: Heparin-coated TDCs were associated with significantly longer failure‑free survival and lower complication rates compared with non‑heparin‑coated catheters.
fields.intervention: Apply a continuous heparin‑bonded coating to the inner lumen and external surface of the tunneled hemodialysis catheter at manufacturing, creating an anticoagulant surface that resists thrombus formation.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained catheter flow patency for ≥ four weeks with no rise in catheter‑related infection incidence.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a prospective, double‑blind RCT enrolling ESRD patients; randomize to heparin‑coated versus standard catheters, monitor daily flow rates, record any occlusion events and infection signs for 28 days, and compare occlusion‑free survival and infection rates between groups.
